title: Observing Atomic-Scale 3D Structural Evolution of Nanocatalysts
content: Platinum-based electrocatalysts are widely used in fuel cells due to their exceptional oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) efficiency. To improve both performance and longevity, researchers have explored alloying with transition metals, doping, and shape engineering to fine-tune key surface and subsurface properties—namely, geometric structure, local chemical environment, and strain. However, fully optimizing these factors remains challenging, as it requires an atomic-level understanding of how they evolve during long-term operation and their direct impact on ORR activity. In this study [3], neural network-assisted atomic electron tomography [1-2] was utilized to investigate the three-dimensional atomic-scale evolution of metal alloy catalysts and its impact on performance degradation. This analysis uncovers significant structural transformations, including reshaping, surface alloying, and strain relaxation, occurring over repeated electrochemical cycling. By systematically analyzing geometry, local chemistry, and strain, ORR activity over thousands of cycles was quantified, establishing a direct correlation between surface doping and catalytic performance [4].
